title: Where factory run probes, and what a broken config does
body:
**Chose:** `factory run` probes after the refuse check, not on the line right after `docs.preflight`; `factory docs preflight` turns a `config.toml` that fails to load into a judge line ("second opinion not probed: …") instead of an error.
**Over:** probing before the refuse check; propagating the config error, which would change preflight's exit code.
**Because:** a refused run prints only its ✗ lines, so a probe there costs a second for nothing; FR-1 says the probe line never changes the exit code.
**Undo:** move the `second_opinion` call above the refuse block in `src/cli/run.rs`; replace the `match` in `preflight::cli` with `?`.

title: The signal handler tracks reviewers in 256 fixed slots
body:
**Chose:** a static array of 256 atomic slots, one per running reviewer, claimed before the spawn and cleared when it ends; a 257th concurrent pass fails with `unreviewed (error: more than 256 reviewers at once)`.
**Over:** a growable registry (needs a lock or allocation, which the signal handler may not touch) or a wait for a free slot (a hidden parallelism cap).
**Because:** the handler must stay async-signal-safe; 256 passes is about 150k changed lines at the 600-line default, far past any diff seen.
**Undo:** raise `SLOTS` in `src/review.rs`.

title: after slice-02
body:
**Covers:** slices 01, 02
**Gate:** 1 run, 0 red, 1.6 min — caught: nothing
**Prove:** FR-1, FR-2 (2/2) — evidence: `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-1-preflight-second-opinion.txt` (logged in → ok line with grok-4.7-high, logged out → judge line naming `cursor-agent login`, exit 0 in text and `--json` both ways), `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-1-review-passes-at-once.txt` (three 2 s passes in 2.11 s, `## Pass 1/2/3` in order)
**Fixed:** none (leaks clean)

title: Where factory review collect writes without --out
body:
**Chose:** without `--out`, `factory review collect` prints the file to stdout and exits 0; the second opinion's `review pass n/m` progress lines go to stderr.
**Over:** a default path (under the data dir or the repo), or making `--out` required.
**Because:** the PRD names no default; stdout keeps the verb pipeable and writes nothing a run would have to clean up, and the hand-checked usage error stays exit 1.
**Undo:** in `collect_file` in `src/cli/review.rs`, replace the `None` arm with a default path or a usage error.

title: The second opinion's findings hold their own ## headings
body: Cursor's findings text has `## ` headings, so a collected file's part cannot end at the next `## `: lift `## Plan` and `## Leaks` up to the next `\n## `, and `## Second opinion` (always last) to the end of the file.

title: Where the driver's collect writes its progress, and how a reuse is matched
body:
**Chose:** the collect's `review pass n/m` lines go to the driver log beside the one `polish: collected … in N s` line, a reuse prints `polish: reused <path> (head <sha>)`, and the driver matches the file's first line against `<!-- head: <lane HEAD> -->` built in `src/closeout.rs` rather than a helper exported from `src/collect.rs`.
**Over:** dropping the pass lines (a 900 s pass would leave the log silent), printing nothing on a reuse, or editing `src/collect.rs` to export the head-line format.
**Because:** the pass lines are the only sign of life during a long collect; `src/collect.rs` belongs to the slice that wrote it.
**Undo:** pass `&mut std::io::sink()` as the progress writer in `collected` in `src/closeout.rs`; move the head-line format into a `pub fn` in `src/collect.rs`.

title: after slice-05
body:
**Covers:** slices 03, 04, 05
**Gate:** 1 runs, 0 red, 1.7 min — caught: nothing
**Prove:** FR-3, FR-5, FR-7 (3/3) — evidence: `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-review-collect.txt` (the real binary on a fixture branch with the stub reviewer: two files → head line, plan, leaks, two counted passes; logged out → `fallback owed`; one 40-line file → `skipped by size` and no stub call; plus the collect tests), `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-collect-two-files.md` (the two-file case's file), `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-polish-collects.txt` (driver log: collected before the first polish spawn, reused before the respawn, no new reviewer call; the first pack's `# Collected` section, identical in the respawn's pack), `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-polish-pack-first.txt` (the first polish pack), `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-gate-0.5.0.txt` and `docs/features/007-polish-in-the-binary/evidence/cp-2-gate.log` (gate green at 0.5.0 with `bundle_lock_matches`, the new polish §1 test and `a_finished_board_polishes_ships_pushes_and_opens_the_draft_pr`; the pack's contract lists `# Collected` between `# Branch` and `# Log`)
**Fixed:** leaks: src/review.rs:560, leaks: src/review.rs:578, leaks: src/review.rs:584 (a file:line cite in a unit test's reviewer text, now "the parser breaks"; inner loop green, 2.1 min)

title: How long the second-opinion probe may take, and whether preflight keeps its log
body:
**Chose:** `review::probe` waits at most 60 s (`PROBE_SECS`), or `[review] timeout_secs` when that is lower; `factory docs preflight` and `factory run` delete the probe's log dir once the line is written.
**Over:** the probe inheriting the 900 s pass timeout, which let a hung `cursor-agent --list-models` hold every preflight and every collect for 15 minutes; keeping one `reviews/<stamp>` dir per preflight, which piles up with no reader.
**Because:** listing the models takes about a second (PRD §3); the preflight line already carries the probe's reason, so its log adds nothing.
**Undo:** set `PROBE_SECS` in `src/review.rs` to the pass timeout; drop the `remove_dir_all` in `preflight::second_opinion`.

title: Does a polish respawn reuse a collect that owes the fallback?
body:
**Chose:** a respawn reuses `collect.md` only when its head line names the lane's HEAD **and** the file neither says `second opinion: fallback owed` nor `verdict: did not run`; otherwise the driver collects again.
**Over:** FR-5's literal rule, reuse whenever the head line matches, which locks a Cursor outage or logout at the first collect into every respawn, including the one after the owner logs in to answer a dead-worker block.
**Because:** the reuse exists to avoid paying Cursor twice; a file where nothing counted paid nothing, and collecting again costs one 1 s probe when Cursor is still out. Found by the local review and the Cursor pass independently. FR-5's acceptance (a logged-in respawn makes no second reviewer call) still holds.
**Undo:** drop the two `!text.contains(…)` conditions in `collected` in `src/closeout.rs`.

title: AD-4 changed
body: Move the collect.md reuse check out of `collected` in `src/closeout.rs` into one `pub fn` in `src/collect.rs`, beside the writer: it takes the file text and the lane HEAD and is true only when the first line is that head line and the file says neither `second opinion: fallback owed` nor `verdict: did not run`. Build those strings from the same source the writer uses, so a wording change cannot silently break reuse. The log lines (pass progress, `polish: reused …`) stay as they are.
